DEFINITION

What is an AI system?

04 / 30

A machine-based system that infers from inputs how to produce predictions, content, recommendations or decisions, with varying autonomy, and outputs that can affect the real world.

Three types of AI you need to know.

Predictive model

Estimates credit risk.

Generative AI

Produces a customer reply.

AI agent

Acts through software tools.

An AI system is a machine-based system that infers from inputs how to produce outputs. Those outputs may be predictions, content, recommendations or decisions, and can affect physical or virtual environments. Systems vary in their autonomy and in whether they adapt after deployment. This is a plain-language paraphrase of the definition used by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, or OECD.

Examples include a model that estimates credit risk, a chatbot that generates replies, and an agent that acts through software tools. For governance, examine how the system is used as well as what the model produces. A recommendation shown to an experienced employee has a different operating context from an automatic customer decision. A supplier's model description therefore needs to be connected to the workflow, data and people in the organisation.
